reason: It's free and portable, so I'll unzip it and throw a card of RAW+JPG at it to see if the speed claims are real. But my culling pipeline can't break, and one dev on 0.4.1 with no plug-in system is not something I make default on a whim.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers and the separate RAW/JPG listing are what would get me to try it, since a 500-shot cull is exactly where IrfanView's 600-900 ms rapid-next hurts. But I would not switch: no plug-ins, no community to ask when something breaks, and a v0.4.1 from one person who may drop it in a year. Setting default for formats by hand in Windows Settings is also a chore I would only do once I trust it.
current_app_pros: IrfanView starts instantly, I know every shortcut by heart, my plug-ins and command-line batch setups are already configured, and it has worked the same way for years. It's tiny and never gets in my way.
current_app_pains: Rapid next/back through big RAW and JPG files lags, RAW support depends on plug-ins and is only so-so, and the UI looks dated. Colour management is not something I fully trust there. It's mild annoyance, not a dealbreaker.
objection: No plug-ins, no big community, hard to find help, and one developer on 0.4.1. If it breaks my cull workflow in the middle of a 500-photo batch I have nobody to ask and no fallback except going back to IrfanView.
would_change_my_mind: A few months of stable releases and visible bug fixes, plus proof that my XMP/sidecar ratings and colour setup survive a cull untouched. Being able to rate or tag and reject in the viewer, with the RAW+JPG pair handled sanely, would make me look seriously.
